# IdeaVim fixtures this host does not match yet.
#
# Generated by VimFixtureReplayTest, which writes the current list to
# build/fixture-failures.txt with the difference for each one, and a header saying how many were
# harvested and why the rest were not. To update this file, read that one and copy the names across
# - never edit a name by hand to make the build pass.
#
# 1044 of the 1047 harvested fixtures pass. Three are left and none of them is a caret: two name an
# IntelliJ action and the third is a piece of machinery nobody has written yet.
#
# The nine that left this list most recently were one bug seen from eight angles plus one that was
# never a bug at all, and both halves are worth recording.
#
# Every multi-caret Visual and Select fixture failed because a blockwise selection put its carets in
# the wrong column and kept carets IdeaVim does not have. A block's caret goes in the *active*
# corner's column - which is the right edge only while the block is being drawn rightwards, so
# `<C-V>jl` read the same either way and `<C-V>bjj` did not - and a line too short to hold the
# block's slice contributes no caret at all. Three more followed from carets that had stopped being
# different carets and were never merged, and one from `vimSelectionStart` defaulting to zero on a
# caret the block had just invented. The details are at each fix; `VsCodeBlockVisualTest` is where
# the numbers live.
#
# The other one was a harness bug, and it is the second of its kind: the harness was harvesting
# tests IdeaVim has `@Disabled`. `search in one time from select mode` sat here as "expected [81],
# actual [82]" when IdeaVim's own caret is at 82 - the test is switched off over there, with the
# note "Ctrl-o doesn't work yet in select mode". `repeat command with execution of ij action` was
# the same, disabled with "This test throws `Recursive runForEachCaret invocations are not
# allowed`", and its entry here blamed the missing IntelliJ action instead. Before believing an
# entry in this file, check that the fixture passes in the plugin.

# --- Two IntelliJ actions, which this host has no equivalent of.
#
# `ideajoin` is IntelliJ's smart join, a language feature this host cannot have: `VjJ` with the
# option set joins the way the language wants rather than the way Vim does.
#
# `partial Action mapping` types `X(EditorToggleCase)` into a half-declared `<Action>` mapping. The
# mapping machinery works - nothing is inserted as literal text, which is what this entry used to
# claim - and `EditorToggleCase` is an IntelliJ action id with no VS Code command behind it. There
# is no toggle-case command; `editor.action.transformToUppercase` and its lowercase twin are the
# whole of what VS Code offers.
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/change/delete/DeleteJoinVisualLinesSpacesActionTest.kt:test join via idea
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/ex/implementation/commands/MapCommandTest.kt:test partial Action mapping

# --- Incsearch for an ex command, which is a different machine from incsearch for `/`.
#
# `:%s/dolor` shows its match and drops the Visual selection while it is still being typed. That
# needs the command line parsed for a range and a pattern before it is run, where previewing `/`
# only ever has a pattern. Nothing about it is host-shaped.
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/group/search/IncsearchTests.kt:test incsearch removes Visual when searching with no Visual range
